finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unvalidated `sort` GET parameter is concatenated directly into the query string. An attacker can inject SQLite expressions (e.g. CASE/subselect boolean-based blind injection) to exfiltrate data from any table in app.db, and can append further clauses. PDO::query with sqlite generally rejects stacked statements, but blind data extraction remains possible.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) in list_users_sorted

trace.note: string concatenated into SQL and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, escaping, or auth check in list_users_sorted. Contrast with list_users_safe (line 10-11), which maps through an allowlist, and find_user (line 16), which uses a prepared statement; those are safe. No other files exist in the repo, so no upstream filter was found.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it unvalidated into the ORDER BY of a PDO::query call; the allowlist exists only in list_users_safe (list.php:10-11), which is a different function. The file has no auth check. One caveat is that nothing in the repo calls list_users_sorted, so whether an anonymous client can actually reach it depends on code outside this repo.
